outline.chapter_title: Foundations of Transformer-Based Language Models and Rotary Position Encoding
outline.description:
This chapter introduces transformer architectures focused on autoregressive language models trained at scale.
It explains why word order information cannot be inferred solely from self–attention scores and introduces positional encodings.
The discussion highlights sine–cosine embeddings pioneered before addressing Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE), its mathematical definition cos(nθᵢ)/sin(nθᵢ) where θᵢ=θ^{−2i/d}, its benefits over absolute indexing, fast computation via matrix multiplication, and its ubiquity across modern LLaMA/Mistral variants.
Finally it presents the practical limitation imposed by a fixed upper bound on sequence length during pretraining.
subtopics: Scale properties tied to dimension index
